equity_bridge.item: Noncontrolling interest (Darling's 50% of Diamond Green Diesel) at book

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle normalisation; no historical CAGR is usable for a crack-spread cyclical
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every CAGR is endpoint-driven by the cycle. Revenue 3yr runs from the FY2022 Russia-shock peak (-11.4%) and 5yr from the FY2020 COVID trough (+13.6%); EPS 3yr -36.1% (FY2022 peak to FY2025 trough) and 5yr undefined (FY2020 loss); owner FCF 3yr -26.5%, 5yr undefined (FY2020 negative). Equity CAGR (1.5% / 6.3%, incl. NCI) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS and is suppressed by $42B of buybacks and dividends since 2021. Selected 1.5% is a long-run nominal volume x price judgment, not a fitted rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (SBC ~$80-117M/yr, 0.1% of revenue), so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are effectively identical; SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. Owner FCF: FY2022 $9,734M, FY2025 $3,864M (OCF 5,826 - investing 1,845 - SBC 117).

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 upswing (tight global product supply, closures in Europe, Australia and California, discounted heavy/sour crude) runs through H2-2026 and eases through 2027 as new Asian/Middle-East capacity (Dangote, Dos Bocas, Yulong) ramps and inventories rebuild. Margins settle at a 6.8% EBITDA mid-cycle (~$10B), above the FY2017-25 nominal average because of structural rationalisation and DGD/SAF earnings under the RFS Set-2 mandate, offset by Benicia's exit and RIN costs on the refining side. Volumes flat-to-slightly-up as Gulf Coast export capacity offsets slow erosion of US gasoline demand.
scenario_narratives.bull: The shortage is structural, not cyclical: no new US capacity in decades, continuing closures abroad and on the West Coast, and diesel/jet demand outrunning supply keep cracks elevated for two more years and the mid-cycle resets to ~8.5% EBITDA (~$13B+), the post-2022 regime rather than the 2017-19 one. RFS Set-2 nearly doubles the biomass-based-diesel mandate and DGD (with Port Arthur SAF) becomes a durable $1B+ earner. This is roughly the sell-side bull view (Goldman $457).
scenario_narratives.bear: Record Q2-2026 margins mean-revert within five quarters, as they did from FY2023 to the Q1-2025 loss: new capacity and a demand slowdown compress cracks to the FY2024-25 run-rate (~5% EBITDA). A future administration or court unwinds the 2026-27 RVO increase or 45Z credit, hitting DGD, while SRE reallocation raises refining compliance cost. EV and efficiency erosion shrinks US gasoline volumes ~1.5%/yr and more high-cost refineries follow Benicia into closure; terminal growth zero.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Valero on what it earns across a refining cycle, not on the quarter it just reported. The TTM to June 2026 contains a record Q2 (13.5% EBITDA margin) and owner FCF of $9.2B, 3.4x the ten-year median; capitalising that would value a peak as if it were permanent. The DCF therefore projects from revenue and an EBITDA-margin path that credits only the guided-strong second half of 2026, then fades to a stated mid-cycle margin by year 4 (base 6.8%, ~$10B EBITDA; bull 8.5%; bear 5.0%). Cyclicality is charged once, through these flows and a 25% bear weight, not again through a stacked discount-rate premium. The market price capitalises a far higher sustained margin than the through-cycle record supports. That gap is the finding; the bull case shows what has to be true to close it.

mid_cycle_normalization.why: Refining is a crack-spread business: EBITDA ranged $0.8B (FY2020) to $18.2B (FY2022) over FY2017-25. TTM owner FCF $9,232M is 3.4x the historical median $2,747M; the base year is the cycle peak.
mid_cycle_normalization.how: Year-1 margin 9.5% (one strong half), 7.5% year 2, 7.0% year 3, 6.8% mid-cycle from year 4; terminal cap 11x owner FCF (~6x EV/EBITDA).
mid_cycle_normalization.sanity_check_note: The multiples check compares the IV against FY2025 trailing EPS, a trough year with a $1.1B impairment, so implied trailing P/E reads high even though the IV is ~11-12x mid-cycle earnings.

key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin is the single dominant assumption: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is ~$1.4-1.5B of EBITDA, roughly $25-30/share in the base case
Crack-spread timing: two more years at Q2-2026 run-rates would add ~$20-30B of cash (~$70-100/share) that the base case fades away
RFS Set-2 / 45Z / LCFS policy reversal (DGD) versus RIN cost on the refining segment
NCI valued at book; if DGD earns more like the bull case the partner's share is worth more than $3.3B
Buyback timing: the flat-count model treats repurchases as value-neutral, but buying back near the top of the 52-week range, at roughly twice the weighted IV, destroys value for continuing holders
Trailing multiples mislead in both directions on a cyclical: the IV looks expensive on trough FY2025 EPS and cheap on peak TTM EPS

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 155.29-419.04
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1035002) for D&A, investing cash flow, impairment, NCI, finance leases, share counts and Q2-2026 balance sheet; VLO_Metrics.csv for revenue, operating income, OCF, debt, cash, SBC and buybacks
data_sources.qualitative: VLO_Analysis.json (Q2-2026 results, FY2026 ~$2B capital-investment guide, $4-5B cash target, $5B buyback authorisation, Benicia closure April 2026, RFS Set-2 rule)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted estimate at 30-Jun-2026, chosen to match the net-debt date: 296.9M basic on 24-Apr-2026 and 287.9M on 24-Jul-2026 (10-Q cover pages) interpolate to ~290M basic at quarter end, plus ~1M dilutive awards (Q2-26 weighted diluted 294M). The 24-Jul count is not used because the cash spent on those July buybacks is still in the 30-Jun balance sheet. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation $117M). VLO does not tag tax withholding on net-share settlement separately; it is inside 'purchases of common stock for treasury' (buybacks). Immaterial at ~0.08% of revenue either way.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 $2,598M; H1-2026 $2,836M; new $5B authorisation July 2026 plus $1.42B remaining. Repurchaser: the flat share count is funded with cash, not a modelling convention.
inputs.fy0_construction: TTM = FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025 (XBRL). Revenue 122,687 + 76,857 - 60,147 = 139,397. Operating income 3,181 + 6,927 - 97 = 10,011; D&A (DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet) 3,158 + 1,577 - 1,505 = 3,230; EBITDA 13,241 = 9.5% margin. The $1,131M Q1-2025 Benicia/Wilmington impairment falls in H1-2025 and drops out of TTM. OCF 5,826 + 6,970 - 1,888 = 10,908; investing outflow 1,845 + 761 - 1,047 = 1,559; reported FCF 9,349 (flattered by working capital on rising product prices). Year 1 of the projection is Jul-2026 to Jun-2027, so H1-2026 cash already sitting in the 30-Jun balance sheet is not counted again in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build: 10-yr UST ~4.3%, beta ~1.1, ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.8%; pre-tax debt ~5.5% (4.3% after tax); debt ~9% of EV at market. WACC ~9.3%, rounded up to 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not again as a discount-rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt, for FINANCE leases: total_debt $11,349M includes ~$2.36B of finance-lease liabilities, so their principal ($268M FY2025) is not deducted from the flows; instead capex_pct carries ~0.2pp of revenue for finance-lease asset renewal. OPERATING leases (~$1.08B liability) stay as US-GAAP operating cost inside EBITDA and are excluded from net debt. One treatment per lease class; nothing charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Diamond Green Diesel is a 50/50 JV with Darling Ingredients that Valero consolidates, so revenue, EBITDA and total debt are 100% of DGD. The partner's share is charged once, in the bridge, at NCI book value $3,267M (30-Jun-2026). Cross-check: NCI income averaged ~$310M/yr FY2018-FY2024 (FY2025 -$102M, H1-2026 +$412M); capitalised at ~10x that is ~$3.1B, close to book. Flows are not also made attributable-only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with MID-CYCLE margin normalisation (routing row: operating company, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of VLO; no prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry. Refining is a crack-spread business: EBITDA (operating income + D&A, ex impairments) ran $5.6B FY2017, $6.6B FY2018, $6.1B FY2019, $0.8B FY2020, $4.5B FY2021, $18.2B FY2022, $14.6B FY2023, $6.5B FY2024, $7.5B FY2025 and $13.2B TTM, with Q2-2026 alone at ~$6.0B (13.5% margin). A peak-quarter or TTM extrapolation is therefore meaningless; the build fades the current upswing over 2-4 years into a stated mid-cycle EBITDA margin. Through-cycle FY2017-FY2025 EBITDA averaged ~$7.8B nominal (~$9.5B in 2026 dollars); base mid-cycle 6.8% on ~$145B revenue is ~$10B, crediting some structural tightening (global closures, no new US capacity) and DGD/SAF growth against the loss of Benicia. Revenue is mostly an oil-price pass-through, so the growth paths are modest and the value driver is the margin path. DATA CAVEAT: the CSV 'EBITDA' column is operating income + a small amortisation item, NOT EBITDA; true D&A (~$3.2B) comes from XBRL DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet and was used here. CSV ShareholdersEquity includes NCI. Interest income not stripped: Valero is net debt, not net cash, and the component build starts from operating income, which excludes other income. Capex: the CSV FCF/CapEx series is blank for FY2025; investing cash outflow (which includes deferred turnaround and catalyst spend and DGD capex) was used, against management's ~$2B FY2026 capital-investment guide. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-10-03): the first build tripped 'implied P/E 27.0x > 2x 10yr avg 13.2x'. Diagnosis: the denominator is FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS (~$7.2), a TROUGH year carrying the $1.1B Benicia/Wilmington impairment and a Q1 loss, so the trip is largely a depressed-denominator artifact rather than peak extrapolation; on mid-cycle EPS (~$16-17: $10B EBITDA less ~$2.9B D&A, ~$0.5B interest, 22% tax, ~$0.3B NCI) the weighted IV is ~11-12x, below the 13.2x 10yr average. The flagged peak_fcf symptom was nevertheless real in year 1 (projected Y1 owner FCF ~$9.6B), so the fade was steepened in all three scenarios (one strong half credited, mid-cycle reached in year 4). Exit caps already bound terminal EV/EBITDA at ~4.5-6.5x, inside history. No WACC premium added: per owner-fcf-adaptations (f), cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight.
inputs.mid_cycle_owner_fcf_note: last_fcf (9,232) is the ACTUAL TTM owner FCF to 30-Jun-2026, kept as the definitional anchor (reported FCF less SBC), and it is a cyclical peak: 3.4x the FY2016-25 median of 2,747 and flattered by working capital. The projection does NOT compound it. Flows are built from base_revenue x an EBITDA-margin path that fades to mid-cycle; the mid-cycle owner FCF is ~$5.1B (6.8% x ~$140B = ~$9.5B EBITDA, less ~22% cash tax on EBIT, ~$2.8B capex, ~$0.13B SBC), which is what the terminal year capitalises (~$5.3-5.4B nominal by year 10).

bear.margin_rationale: Steepened 2026-10-03: 7.0% year 1 (was 8.5%) so the record quarter mean-reverts inside the first projection year, then 5.0% (FY2024-25 run-rate).

base.margin_rationale: Sanity-check fix 2026-10-03: fade steepened so year 1 is not anchored at the Q2-2026 peak. Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) 9.5% (was 10.5%) credits only one strong half (H2-2026, guided 'constructive') before 2027 normalises; 7.5% year 2 (was 8.5%), 7.0% year 3, and the 6.8% mid-cycle (~$10B EBITDA) is reached in year 4 instead of year 5. The mid-cycle level itself is unchanged: it is already the through-cycle FY2017-FY2025 average restated to 2026 dollars, not a peak run-rate.
base.capex_rationale: ~$2B capital-investment guide plus ~0.2pp finance-lease renewal; D&A (inflated by turnaround amortisation and Benicia accelerated depreciation) converges to capex at 2.0% so the terminal year carries no perpetual excess-depreciation tax shield.
base.tax_rationale: 21% federal plus state and foreign (Canada, UK, Ireland) ~22% cash rate; FY2022-23 cash taxes ran ~22-25% of pretax income in strong years.
base.wc_rationale: Revenue is mostly an oil-price pass-through; receivables + LIFO inventory exceed payables modestly, so growth consumes a little cash (-3% of the revenue change).
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: Cap is on terminal owner FCF (TV/FCF_N), not EBITDA. Base 11x FCF on a 6.8% mid-cycle margin is ~6x terminal EV/EBITDA; bull 12x on 8.5% ~6.5x; bear 9x on 5.0% ~4.5x. All sit inside VLO's own FY2016-FY2025 range (3.6x-19.3x on the sanity check's basis, whose 'EBITDA' is CSV operating income, i.e. really EV/EBIT) and below its 11.2x average, so the terminal value cannot imply a multiple outside history. Bear floor deliberately NOT set at the 3.6x FY2022 minimum: that was a peak-earnings denominator, not a distressed valuation.

bull.margin_rationale: Steepened 2026-10-03 with the base: 11.5% / 10.0% / 9.0% (was 12.5 / 11.0 / 9.5), reaching the 8.5% structural mid-cycle in year 4.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 11x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the valuation is struck one quarter after a record quarter, with the stock up ~98% YTD and at the top of its 52-week range (155-419), which is historically where refiner margins mean-revert and policy risk on RINs/45Z cuts against the refining segment. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold together, a structural (not cyclical) reset of crack spreads and a durable RFS/45Z regime for DGD. Base at 50% is the through-cycle normalisation.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
sanity_check.fix_applied: Mid-cycle normalisation tightened (2026-10-03). Original trip: implied P/E 27.0x > 2x 10yr avg 13.2x (diagnosis peak_fcf: TTM owner FCF 9,232 = 3.4x median 2,747). Fix: EBITDA-margin fade steepened in all scenarios so year 1 credits only the guided-strong H2-2026 and mid-cycle is reached in year 4 (base 10.5/8.5/7.5/7.0 -> 9.5/7.5/7.0/6.8; bull 12.5/11.0/9.5/8.8 -> 11.5/10.0/9.0/8.5; bear 8.5/5.5 -> 7.0/5.0); mid-cycle levels unchanged. Exit caps (11x/12x/9x terminal owner FCF = ~6x/6.5x/4.5x EV/EBITDA) already inside the historical EV/EBITDA range, left unchanged. No WACC premium (risk charged once, in flows + 25% bear weight). Weighted IV 195.53 -> 187.68. Residual note: the P/E denominator is FY2025 EPS (~$7.2), a trough/impairment year; on mid-cycle EPS (~$16-17) the IV is ~11-12x.
